newsitem.title: FRANCE: Human rights judge says Bosnia mission lacks funds.
newsitem.headline: Human rights judge says Bosnia mission lacks funds.

text.p: Lack of funds is undermining an international group of judges meant to monitor human rights in Bosnia, an Austrian member of the mission said on Wednesday.
"If western governments want to reinforce human rights in Bosnia-Herzegovina, they should supply the means," Manfred Nowak, a member of the 14-judge chamber of human rights for Bosnia, told Reuters.

The chamber, most of whose members are appointed by the Strasbourg-based Council of Europe under the terms of the Dayton peace accord ending the 1992-95 war, was in theory to be funded by Bosnia itself.
"Everyone knew from the start that western governments would have to pay...Bosnia is destroyed. It can't pay," he said.

The Danish government contributed $1 million that allowed the group to keep going until January 1997. Since then, the 14 judges, who meet once a month, had received neither pay nor expenses, Nowak said.
"It's a threat to the independence of justice," Nowak said. He estimated the chamber required four to five million deutschemarks ($2.3 to $2.9 million) a year to operate properly.
The head of the chamber, Denmark's Peter Germer, announced last month he plans to resign in July in protest at the lack of funds.
The human rights commission of the 40-member Council of Europe, acting with the mediation of the chamber, has opened 1,317 provisional dossiers into human rights violations in Bosnia.
